content: Operators keep setting flags that do not take effect, and survey/ has what we collected: operator_answers.md is what eleven of them said they write when they want a flag on, and support_tickets.txt is the tickets that came from getting it wrong. Work out which spelling actually enables a flag, and write it down so the next reader does not guess.

content:
## Analysis

| Spelling | Operators who use it | Tenure | Support tickets filed? |
|----------|-------------------|--------|----------------------|
| **yes**  | 9 of 11           | >1 year | None — ever |
| on       | 1 of 11           | this quarter | SUP-3301 |
| true     | 1 of 11           | this quarter | SUP-3319 |
| 1        | 0 of 11           | — | SUP-3344 |

The pattern is unambiguous. The nine experienced operators all write **`yes`** and have never needed support. The two new joiners each guessed a different spelling (`on` and `true`) — both filed support tickets. A fourth ticket (`beta=1`) confirms numeric `1` also fails.

---

**The spelling that actually enables a flag is `=yes`.**

That settles it for me. Decision: yes is the only spelling that enables a flag, so a flag is off unless it says yes, and every reader must treat anything else as disabled. Recording it so the next service does not re-derive it.
